articles.title: ‘I’ll Gouge Out Your Eyes’: Mau Railway Parcel Superintendent Threatens RPF Jawan, Video Sparks Row
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mau (Uttar Pradesh): A 1 minute 45 second video from the railway parcel office in Mau, dated February 10, has surfaced on social media showing a heated altercation between the Railway Parcel Superintendent and an RPF jawan.

body.html:
Mau (Uttar Pradesh): A 1 minute 45 second video from the railway parcel office in Mau, dated February 10, has surfaced on social media showing a heated altercation between the Railway Parcel Superintendent and an RPF jawan.

In the viral video, a man identified as Rajesh Singh, Parcel Superintendent of Mau, is seen publicly threatening and verbally abusing an RPF constable. Wearing glasses, Singh loudly declares his name and position and, in Bhojpuri, threatens to gouge out the jawan’s eyes. “It will take two minutes to gouge out the eyes. Don’t you know who you’re talking to? Your parcel will go before the parcel,” he is heard saying. He is also seen using abusive language.

The RPF constable has been identified as Amit Kumar Yadav, currently posted in Chhattisgarh and originally from Mau. According to reports, around 4:30 pm on Tuesday, he visited the railway parcel office to book a parcel. The parcel was reportedly open, and Superintendent Rajesh Singh asked him to pack it properly before booking. However, Amit allegedly insisted on sending it unpacked.

During the exchange, Amit stated that he was in the RPF and would handle any issues related to the open parcel. In response, Rajesh Singh reportedly said he had served 15 years in the RPF before being transferred to the parcel department and asked him not to “explain” the rules. The argument escalated, and Singh allegedly began shouting, threatening and attempting to assault the jawan, while the latter repeatedly asked him to speak properly.

GRP officials stated that upon noticing the commotion, officers reached the spot and called both parties to the office. After hearing both sides, a compromise was reportedly reached with the intervention of higher authorities. Despite the settlement, the RPF jawan shared the video on social media later that night, following which it went viral.

The incident has triggered debate online, with some users linking it to a recent controversy in Kanpur involving an HDFC Bank employee who was accused of threatening and abusing a customer.

articles.title: Poisoned, Robbed, Then Thrown Off Bus? CCTV from Nainital Sparks Outrage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Haldwani (Uttarakhand): A disturbing incident has surfaced from Haldwani, raising serious questions over the conduct of roadways bus staff.

body.html:
Haldwani (Uttarakhand): A disturbing incident has surfaced from Haldwani, raising serious questions over the conduct of roadways bus staff. A young man, identified as Pankaj Pandey from Pithoragarh, was allegedly drugged, robbed and later thrown off a moving bus while travelling from Delhi to Nainital.

According to reports, Pankaj was targeted by a drugging gang during his journey from Delhi to Haldwani. He was allegedly administered intoxicants and robbed of his mobile phone and cash. It is further alleged that the gang forced him to carry out an online transaction of nearly ₹1 lakh.

The incident took a shocking turn when the bus, en route from Haldwani to Nainital, was stopped near Kathgodam. Pankaj, who was reportedly unconscious at the time, was pushed off the roadways bus and fell onto the road.

CCTV footage shows the youth attempting to get up after the fall but failing due to his condition. Early morning walkers noticed him lying unconscious on the roadside and immediately alerted the police.

Police reached the spot and shifted Pankaj to a hospital for treatment. During preliminary investigation, it emerged that he had been thrown off the bus. A video related to the incident has since gone viral on social media, triggering widespread outrage.

The driver and conductor of the roadways bus are facing sharp criticism, with many questioning why medical assistance was not provided instead of abandoning an unconscious passenger on the road.

Police have launched a detailed investigation. Efforts are underway to trace the alleged drugging gang, while the role of the roadways staff is also being examined.

(Updated 12 Feb 2026)

articles.title: Divyang Beggar Thrashed Inside Mirzapur Temple Complex; Inspector Suspended After Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video from the Maa Vindhyavasini temple complex in Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, has surfaced on social media, showing a police officer allegedly beating a disabled man who was begging on the premises.

body.html:
A video from the Maa Vindhyavasini temple complex in Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, has surfaced on social media, showing a police officer allegedly beating a disabled man who was begging on the premises. In the video, the man can be heard pleading for help while the officer continues to strike him with a stick. The incident was filmed by a bystander and later went viral online.

According to police, the disabled man was begging near Gate No. 2 of the temple and was allegedly intoxicated. Officials stated that following complaints from visitors, efforts were being made to remove him from the temple premises. During the process, a scuffle reportedly broke out between the man and the police personnel.

Taking cognisance of the viral video, Superintendent of Police Archana Rajat Kaushik suspended Inspector Sunil Kumar Rai and attached him to the police lines. A report has been sought from the City Commissioner within three days.

Police also stated that an attempt was made to record the statement of the disabled man regarding the incident, but it was unsuccessful.

The video has once again raised serious questions about police conduct and handling of vulnerable individuals in public places.

articles.title: Jaunpur: Two Serving Constables Suspended for Allegedly Stealing ₹1.62 Lakh iPhone from Showroom
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Two serving police constables in Jaunpur have been suspended after CCTV footage allegedly captured them stealing an expensive iPhone from a mobile showroom in the Line Bazar police station area. The incident took place on February 7 at around 2 p.m.

body.html:
Two serving police constables in Jaunpur have been suspended after CCTV footage allegedly captured them stealing an expensive iPhone from a mobile showroom in the Line Bazar police station area.

The incident took place on February 7 at around 2 p.m. at a mobile showroom near JC’s intersection. According to shop owner Shivam, the two constables entered the store posing as customers and asked a female staff member to show them various iPhone models. They reportedly spent nearly 20 minutes examining the phones before saying they were not interested and leaving the shop.

Old Phone Left Behind, New One Missing

Later, the shop owner noticed that an iPhone 15 Max worth ₹1.62 lakh was missing. Upon reviewing the CCTV footage, he allegedly saw one of the constables slipping the new phone into his pocket while leaving behind his old iPhone 13 Pro as a decoy.

Shivam shared the CCTV clip in a WhatsApp group with around 200 people, after which the individuals were identified as police personnel. He then filed a written complaint and personally met the City Superintendent of Police, presenting the footage.

Phone Recovered, Inquiry Ordered

Based on the complaint, a case was registered and an investigation was launched. The stolen phone was recovered on Sunday and returned to the shop owner.

Shivam also informed police that one of the accused constables had previously frequented the area and had studied at a digital library operating above his shop about a year ago.

City SP Ayush Srivastava confirmed that both constables — Dhananjay Bind and Mithilesh Yadav — have been suspended with immediate effect.

“Orders have been issued for a departmental inquiry against both personnel,” the SP said.

Further investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Indore: Three Youths Arrested for Urinating Near Hanuman Temple While Intoxicated, Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Police in Indore arrested three youths for allegedly urinating near a Hanuman temple while under the influence of alcohol in the Moti Tabeela area, which falls under the Raoji Bazaar police station limits.

body.html:
Police in Indore arrested three youths for allegedly urinating near a Hanuman temple while under the influence of alcohol in the Moti Tabeela area, which falls under the Raoji Bazaar police station limits. The action was taken after a video of the incident surfaced on social media, triggering public outrage.

According to reports, the incident occurred on Saturday, when the three youths were allegedly involved in indecent behaviour outside the temple. Following the circulation of the video, Vishwa Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal activist Tannu Sharma lodged a complaint with the police and demanded strict action. Bajrang Dal activists also warned that they would take action if police failed to act within 24 hours.

Based on the viral video and CCTV footage provided by local residents, police identified and arrested Arpit Chauhan, Raja Dubey, and Kamal Ahirwar on Sunday. The accused were booked under restrictive sections, and further legal proceedings are underway.

During questioning, the youths admitted their mistake, held their ears, and apologised at the police station, stating that they were intoxicated at the time. They assured police that they would not repeat such behaviour and expressed regret if religious sentiments were hurt.

Police said the matter is being dealt with seriously to prevent such incidents in the future.

articles.title: Mall Turns Battleground as Wife Confronts Husband’s Girlfriend in Sonbhadra, Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident has surfaced from Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh, where a fierce scuffle between two women broke out at Citycart Shopping Mall on Civil Line Road, creating chaos inside the mall. A video of the incident is now going viral on social media.

body.html:
A shocking incident has surfaced from Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh, where a fierce scuffle between two women broke out at Citycart Shopping Mall on Civil Line Road, creating chaos inside the mall. A video of the incident is now going viral on social media.

According to eyewitnesses, a young man was shopping with his girlfriend at the mall when his wife suddenly arrived. This led to a heated argument, which quickly escalated into a physical fight between the two women. Amid the chaos, the young man fled the spot, leaving both women engaged in a prolonged scuffle.

The incident took place within the jurisdiction of Robertsganj Kotwali police station. The viral video shows the two women attacking each other, while several people stood by and recorded the incident on their mobile phones instead of intervening.

After some time, onlookers managed to separate the two women. The video also shows injuries on one woman’s hand, with claims that she was bitten during the altercation, though this has not been officially confirmed.

The incident caused panic and disruption inside the mall and has since become a major topic of discussion on social media, raising questions about public safety and bystander behaviour.

Police have not yet issued a detailed statement regarding the viral video or any formal complaint.

articles.title: 40 Patients Attempt Escape from Govt De-Addiction Centre in Mohali’s Sector 66
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident was reported from Sector 66, Mohali, where around 40 patients attempted to escape from a government-run drug de-addiction centre on Monday afternoon.

body.html:
A shocking incident was reported from Sector 66, Mohali, where around 40 patients attempted to escape from a government-run drug de-addiction centre on Monday afternoon.

According to officials, the incident occurred at around 3:15 pm when patients gathered during treatment and tried to force open a wooden door to flee the facility. Sensing the danger, security guards immediately locked the door from outside, preventing it from opening despite repeated attempts by the patients.

Meanwhile, two police personnel deployed at the centre shifted the patients to the rear ward and secured the iron gate, bringing the situation under control. Police were informed, and a daily diary (DDR) entry has been registered.

Officials said that doctors and staff were present outside at the time of the incident. They added that had the door opened, patients could have escaped and posed serious risks to public and staff safety.

Staff members revealed that many patients are booked under the NDPS Act and have a history of escape attempts. They warned that such incidents endanger the lives of doctors, guards, and staff. Currently, only two police personnel are deployed for security at the centre.

They also recalled a previous incident where patients created a ruckus at night, attacked security guards, and two patients allegedly escaped through the roof.

Officials explained that earlier, patients were admitted to de-addiction centres voluntarily and were free to leave. However, under the Punjab government’s “War Against Drugs” campaign, drug users booked under Section 27 of the NDPS Act are now sent to de-addiction centres for treatment instead of jail, leading to increased unrest during treatment.

Phase 11 SHO Aman Singh clarified that no patient escaped, only an attempt was made. He said patients often become irritable when medication dosages are reduced during treatment. He assured that the police are providing full support for staff safety and stressed the need for experienced and patient handling in such cases.

articles.excerpt: In a shocking incident at a grocery store on Railway Road, Sadar Bazaar, a man identified as Ashwini (alias Ashu Bhatia) was caught red-handed stealing premium items.

body.html:
In a shocking incident at a grocery store on Railway Road, Sadar Bazaar, a man identified as Ashwini (alias Ashu Bhatia) was caught red-handed stealing premium items. Despite recently returning from a month-long trip to Australia on a tourist visa, the Moti Nagar resident was found hiding expensive cow ghee, honey, and ketchup inside his clothes.

Key Highlights:
The Modus Operandi: The suspect attempted to pay for a single packet of Maggi while concealing over ₹3,000 worth of groceries in his pants.

The Sting: Store employees had been tracking him via CCTV for days after noticing previous thefts of tea leaves.

The Confession: On video, the accused admitted to multiple thefts across Sadar Bazaar and Meerut Road, citing vague "financial difficulties."

Police Action: Sadar Bazaar police have taken the suspect into custody along with the video evidence.

articles.title: “I Am a Thakur and I’m Proud”: HDFC Bank Employee Issues Clarification After Viral Video in Kanpur
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A female bank employee at an HDFC Bank branch in Kanpur, whose video went viral over an alleged altercation, has issued a clarification, claiming the clip is being circulated in a misleading context.

body.html:
A female bank employee at an HDFC Bank branch in Kanpur, whose video went viral over an alleged altercation, has issued a clarification, claiming the clip is being circulated in a misleading context.

Relationship Manager Aastha Singh, posted at the HDFC Bank branch in Panki, released a video statement with folded hands, saying she never misbehaved with any customer. She stated that the dispute was with the husband of a female contractual employee and not with a customer.

According to Aastha, the incident dates back to January 6. She said the contractual employee had resigned and wanted to be relieved the same day, while her sister-in-law remained present at the branch for hours, leading to a minor argument. Later in the evening, the employee’s husband allegedly came to the bank, used abusive language, questioned Aastha about her caste, and issued threats.

“I was angered after being asked about my caste and spoken to rudely. I stand by my statement even today. I am a Thakur, and I am proud of it,” Aastha said, adding that some of her words could have been chosen more carefully.

The viral video shows her allegedly abusing and attempting to attack someone with a laptop. Aastha claimed the footage is being portrayed as a caste-related issue, which she denied. She said she has informed her seniors through an internal email and is considering legal action.

Speaking to the media, Aastha also alleged that after the video went viral, she has been subjected to online abuse, including threats of rape and physical harm. “I am becoming famous in the wrong way,” she said, adding that she may file a defamation case.

Police or bank authorities have not yet issued an official statement on the matter.
